title: Personalized Management of Erdheim-Chester Disease: The Pivotal Role of Molecular and Cross-Sectional Imaging from Staging to Targeted Therapy Monitoring.
abstract: Erdheim-Chester disease (ECD) is a rare, clonal non-Langerhans cell histiocytic neoplasm driven by activating mutations in the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway, most notably the BRAF-V600E mutation. The discovery of these molecular alterations has shifted the therapeutic paradigm from non-specific immunosuppression to personalized targeted therapies, such as BRAF and MEK inhibitors, dramatically improving patient outcomes. Given its protean and insidious systemic manifestations, imaging plays an indispensable role in the personalized diagnostic and therapeutic pathway of ECD. Metadiaphyseal symmetrical osteosclerosis represents the skeletal hallmark, while extraskeletal involvement typically affects the cardiovascular, retroperitoneal, pulmonary, and central nervous systems, yielding pathognomonic imaging signatures such as the "coated aorta" and "hairy kidney." Advanced cross-sectional techniques-including CT, MRI, and organ-specific mapping protocols-are crucial for baseline phenotype characterization, risk stratification, and guiding biopsies toward hypermetabolic sites for biomarker detection. Furthermore, molecular imaging with 18F-FDG PET/CT has emerged as the cornerstone for baseline systemic staging and quantitative metabolic response monitoring via PERCIST criteria, enabling early assessment of targeted treatment efficacy long before morphological changes occur. This review illustrates the multimodality imaging spectrum of ECD based on our institutional experience, emphasizing how precision imaging integrates with molecular profiling to guide personalized patient management.

title: Self-Monitoring Theranostic Nanomaterials for Biomedical Imaging and Cancer Therapy: Real-Time Visualization of Biodistribution, Payload Release, and Therapeutic Response.
abstract: Theranostic nanomedicines integrate therapeutic delivery with diagnostic imaging, but many conventional platforms primarily visualize nanocarrier localization and provide limited information on whether the therapeutic payload has been released, the intended treatment mechanism has been activated, or a meaningful biological response has occurred. Self-monitoring theranostic nanomedicines have emerged as functionally informative platforms capable of reporting their own biodistribution, biological fate, payload release, therapeutic activation, and downstream response in real time or through longitudinal imaging. This review summarizes the conceptual framework and design principles of self-monitoring nanomedicine, including always-on and activatable probes, Förster resonance energy transfer, self-quenching and dequenching mechanisms, ratiometric sensing, environment-responsive contrast agents, and multimodal imaging. Major imaging modalities, including fluorescence, magnetic resonance, photoacoustics, positron emission tomography, single-photon emission computed tomography, computed tomography, and ultrasound imaging, are discussed with emphasis on their respective capabilities and limitations for monitoring nanomedicine performance. Representative studies demonstrate the visualization of systemic biodistribution, target-site accumulation, carrier disassembly, drug and nucleic-acid release, photothermal and photodynamic activation, gene and RNA activity, oxidative stress, immune modulation, apoptosis, and pathogen clearance. Particular emphasis is placed on cancer theranostics, where self-monitoring nanomaterials can integrate tumor imaging with the assessment of intratumoral delivery, payload release, therapeutic activation, and early treatment response. Broader applications in inflammatory and immune-related diseases and infectious diseases further illustrate the general applicability of these monitoring principles beyond cancer. Despite substantial progress, clinical translation remains limited by ambiguous signal interpretation, insufficient quantitative validation, biological safety concerns, manufacturing complexity, and regulatory challenges. title: Occurrence of Microplastics and Potentially Toxic Elements in Red Sea Crab (Portunus pelagicus) and Squid (Uroteuthis spp.): Contamination and Food-Safety Concerns.
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) and potentially toxic elements (PTEs) are co-occurring marine contaminants, yet integrated assessments of Red Sea seafood remain limited. This study evaluated MP contamination, PTE bioaccumulation, and dietary health risks in Portunus pelagicus (n = 281) and Uroteuthis spp. (n = 159) from Yanbu, Rabigh, and Umluj. A standardized subset of 180 specimens was examined for MPs using stereomicroscopy, yielding 508 suspected particles. All 508 particles were examined by FTIR, of which 260 (51.2%) were spectroscopically confirmed as polyethylene (PE), while 248 (48.8%) remained unconfirmed. Crabs showed approximately 10-89-fold higher suspected-particle burdens than squid (0.742-1.683 vs. 0.008-0.167 particles/g wet weight). Eleven PTEs were quantified in edible muscle by ICP-MS. Squid contained approximately 17-24-fold higher Fe and 5-7-fold higher Cd, whereas crabs contained 11-13-fold higher total As and higher Zn. Non-carcinogenic risk remained below the conventional threshold (HI < 1) across all scenarios, whereas estimated arsenic-related carcinogenic risk exceeded 1 × 10-4 in some crab-consumption scenarios under the assumed 7% inorganic-As fraction. Exploratory MP-PTE associations were strongly influenced by species identity and cannot establish MP-mediated PTE transfer.

title: Organ-specific depth of response to CD19-directed CAR T-cell therapy in B-cell lymphomas.
mesh: Humans; Female; Male; Retrospective Studies; Middle Aged; Aged; Antigens, CD19; Immunotherapy, Adoptive; Lymphoma, B-Cell; Receptors, Chimeric Antigen
abstract: BACKGROUND: CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor T cell therapy (CART) has transformed treatment of relapsed or refractory (r/r) large B cell lymphoma (LBCL); however, organ-specific response patterns and depth of response (DoR) remain insufficiently characterized. This study evaluated organ-specific imaging response and the impact of spatial disease patterns on progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, 109 consecutive patients with r/r LBCL treated with CD19-directed CART between January 2019 and May 2025 were included. Baseline and follow-up CT or PET/CT was analyzed using structured lesion tracking. Up to six target lesions per patient were assessed according to Lugano criteria, and the sum of the products of diameters (SPD) was calculated. DoR was defined as percentage change in SPD from baseline. Associations with PFS and OS were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression. RESULTS: Among 109 patients (median age, 65 years [IQR, 57-71]), 65 (59.6%) had extranodal disease at baseline. Baseline tumor burden was higher in patients with extranodal than nodal disease (median SPD, 3573 mm2 [IQR, 1314-9708] versus 1998 mm2 [IQR, 1347-2921]). DoR was comparable between nodal and extranodal lesions at both time points (- 62.1% vs. - 65.6% and - 77.9% vs. - 78.1%); this comparability at the second follow-up may partly reflect differential attrition, as extranodal patients were more likely to be lost to follow-up before this timepoint. Despite similar tumor reduction, median PFS was 306.5 days in nodal versus 90 days in extranodal disease. Baseline tumor burden (SPD) was independently associated with both PFS and OS (HR per doubling of SPD 1.17 and 1.21, respectively). Pleural, hepatobiliary, and adrenal involvement showed the strongest associations with adverse outcomes in this exploratory, hypothesis-generating organ-level analysis; pleural involvement remained independently associated with PFS and OS, though organ-specific subgroups were small (n = 7-19) and estimates should be interpreted with caution. CONCLUSION: Tumor reduction occurs in nodal and extranodal disease after CART, but outcomes depend on anatomical disease distribution. title: Assessment of Microplastic and Element Contamination in Fish Sold by Informal Roadside Vendors in Limpopo Province, South Africa.
mesh: South Africa; Animals; Food Contamination; Water Pollutants, Chemical; Microplastics; Fishes; Environmental Monitoring; Seafood
abstract: Fish is the cheapest source of protein, minerals, and vitamins for most households in sub-Saharan Africa. Of late, microplastic and metal pollution have raised concerns about food safety, especially in informal markets where fish is commonly sold and consumed. Informal roadside fish markets are, however, almost absent from this literature, and the extent to which post harvest handling adds to the contaminant load of the tissue that is actually eaten is unknown. This study assessed microplastic and element contamination in ready to eat braaied (open fire grilled) fish sold by roadside vendors in Thohoyandou, Limpopo Province, South Africa. Fish samples (n = 4 per stall) were collected from nine stalls, and microplastics extracted from the dorsolateral white muscle were characterised by morphology, colour and polymer type using stereomicroscopy and micro-Fourier transform infrared (µ-FTIR) spectroscopy, while element concentrations in the same tissue were determined by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) following microwave assisted acid digestion. The study indicates high microplastic burdens, dominated by fibres, films, and fragments. Total microplastic abundances differed significantly among sites, with mean values ranging from ~ 105 particles kg- 1 at site 9 to ~ 470 particles kg- 1 at site 1. Transparent microplastics dominated, and colours such as black, blue, red, yellow, green and other occurred at much lower concentrations. Polymer identification by µ-FTIR showed that polyethylene (40.5%), polypropylene (23.8%), polystyrene (18.3%) and polyvinyl chloride (7.4%) accounted for most of the particles analysed. Iron (Fe) was the dominant trace element, showing the highest mean concentrations across all sites (~ 70-110 mg kg-1). The concentrations of the 12 elements recorded in braaied fish from roadside vendors varied among sites, and mean Cr, Cu, Se and Mo concentrations exceeded FAO/WHO recommended maximum levels for fish at several stalls. Estimated consumer intake ranged from ~ 180 to ~ 790 particles per meal (~ 2-12 particles kg- 1 body weight), with the highest values at stalls adjacent to busy roads. There is a need for improved hygiene practices, better control of plastic pollution, and enhanced food safety monitoring in informal fish markets in South Africa.

title: Discrepant responses of abundant and rare taxa to polyethylene microplastic and nanoplastic perturbations in cold seep sediment.
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) and nanoplastics (NPs) are emerging contaminants in deep-sea ecosystems, yet their specific impacts on the internal heterogeneity of cold seep microbiomes remain poorly understood. Here, microcosm experiments with cold seep sediments exposed to polyethylene particles were conducted to investigate the response patterns of abundant and rare taxa to MP/NP-induced disturbances. The results indicated that MPs/NPs exposure reshaped bacterial community structure, with significant enrichment of Epsilonbacteraeota, a phylum associated with chemoautotrophic metabolism. In contrast, archaeal alpha diversity showed no significant response to MPs/NPs exposure. Abundant and rare taxa exhibited contrasting responses in community composition, assembly patterns, and network associations. Despite stochastic processes largely governing overall community assembly, the assembly mechanism of rare bacteria shifted toward heterogeneous selection under NPs exposure, which contrasted sharply with the homogeneous selection observed in the rare archaea. Furthermore, network analysis revealed that rare taxa constituted the majority of nodes in both co-occurrence networks. Functional predictions suggested contrasting responses, with lower relative abundances of taxa assigned to sulfate respiration in abundant bacteria under most treatments and higher relative abundances of taxa assigned to sulfur oxidation and nitrogen cycling in rare taxa under some treatments. Overall, this study highlights the contrasting responses of abundant and rare taxa to MPs/NPs exposure and provides insights for assessing the ecological risks of plastic pollution in deep-sea environments.

title: Ferro-Immuno-Structural Axis (FISA): Kidney specific microplastic toxicity via TLR18 centric immunosuppression and iron dyshomeostasis in rainbow trout.
journal: Comp Biochem Physiol Part D Genomics Proteomics (2026)
abstract: Toll-like receptors (TLRs) are central to innate immunity, yet the expanded TLR repertoire in teleost fish and its tissue-specific response to microplastic (MP) stress remain poorly understood. We performed an integrated genome-wide analysis of the TLR family in rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) and conducted multi-tissue transcriptomic profiling (kidney, intestine, liver, muscle, brain, and gill) following MP exposure (500 μg/L). The rainbow trout genome contains 21 TLR members, including six TLR13 paralogs and fish-specific TLR18. Multi-tissue transcriptomics revealed kidney-specific TLR18 centric immunosuppression: TLR18 was exclusively and dramatically downregulated (log2FC = -2.90, P = 1.22 × 10-11), accompanied by suppression of TLR8, TLR13, TLR21, and TLR3. The trafficking regulator unc93b1 (-2.69, P = 1.66 × 10-8) and downstream nodes IRF2, JAK1, TRAF2, and RELA/p65 were all significantly inhibited, indicating pathway-level silencing. Notably, fth1a exhibited extreme kidney-specific upregulation (log2FC = 16.99, P = 5.18 × 10-25) but downregulation in other tissues, revealing ferroptosis-like iron dyshomeostasis. Heat shock proteins collapsed comprehensively (6/6 members, P < 0.05), coupled with glomerular filtration barrier damage (col4a1/6, nphs2, wt1). These correlational data support a hypothetical Ferro-Immuno-Structural Axis (FISA) model that may integrate kidney specific microplastic toxicity through TLR18 centric immunosuppression, iron dyshomeostasis, and structural disintegration.

title: Reirradiation for prostate cancer local recurrence: State of the art and future directions.
abstract: Local recurrence after curative radiation therapy or postoperative radiotherapy for prostate cancer remains a challenging clinical scenario, requiring careful evaluation to balance disease control with the risk of treatment-related adverse events. Reirradiation has progressively emerged as a clinically meaningful salvage option for appropriately selected patients with localized recurrence. The widespread implementation of multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging and prostate-specific membrane antigen positron emission tomography-computed tomography has transformed clinical decision-making by enabling earlier detection of recurrence, more accurate localization of disease, and improved identification of patients who may benefit from focal salvage approaches. In this setting, multidisciplinary evaluation and careful patient selection are essential. Among available reirradiation techniques, photon-based stereotactic body radiotherapy currently has the largest body of supporting clinical evidence, while brachytherapy remains a valid alternative in experienced centers and protontherapy may offer additional opportunities to improve dose conformity in selected cases. Although oncological outcomes are encouraging, the available evidence remains predominantly retrospective and heterogeneous, highlighting the need for prospective studies and standardized treatment strategies. This commentary synthesizes contemporary evidence on re-irradiation for locally recurrent prostate cancer after both definitive and postoperative radiation therapy, with a particular focus on patient selection, treatment techniques, oncological outcomes, treatment-related adverse events, and emerging future directions.

title: Engineering ruthenium catalyst inside hollow mesoporous silica nanoreactors via flash nanoprecipitation for selective hydrogenation of furfural.
abstract: Ru nanoparticles supported on polystyrene-block-poly(acrylic acid) (Ru@PS-PAA) was constructed via a flash nanoprecipitation (FNP) strategy. Subsequently, Ru nanoparticles confined in hollow-mesoporous SiO2 (Ru@SiO2) was obtained with Ru@PS-PAA as precursor. Ru@PS-PAA exhibited high selectivity toward furfural‑hydrogenation achieving 98% yield of furfuryl-alcohol. In contrast, Ru@SiO2 promoted consecutive hydrogenation of aldehyde-group and furan-ring of furfural to quantitatively afford tetrahydrofurfuryl-alcohol in 97% yield under identical conditions. The polymeric confinement in Ru@PS-PAA provides a soft and flexible microenvironment that stabilizes Ru nanoparticles, regulates the residence and diffusion of furfural for its selective CO bond hydrogenation. In contrast, the hollow-mesoporous SiO2 nanoreactor of Ru@SiO2 offers a rigid confined-cavity that enriches furfural and furfuryl-alcohol around Ru active-sites, prolongs their residence time, and facilitates consecutive hydrogenation-pathway toward tetrahydrofurfuryl-alcohol. This work highlights the potential of FNP as a versatile platform for constructing high-performance heterogeneous-catalysts with controllable size, morphology and confined structures.

title: Imaging biomarkers related to 18F-FDG PET/CT for predicting microvascular invasion in hepatocellular carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: This study, through a meta-analysis, aimed to assess the predictive performance of 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) for microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). METHODS: Web of Science, Embase, PubMed, and Cochrane Library were comprehensively searched from database inception to January 13, 2026. EndNote 21was employed for literature screening and data extraction. Meta-analysis was carried out on the extracted data using Stata 15, MetaDisc 1.4, and MedCalc. RESULTS: In total, 21 studies were included, involving 2,023 patients with HCC, of whom 890 were MVI+ and 1,133 were MVI-. In univariable analyses, both tumor-to-normal liver uptake ratio (TLR) (odds ratio [OR] = 2.577, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.446-4.593, P = 0.001) and maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) (OR = 1.272, 95% CI: 1.036-1.561, P = 0.021) were significantly associated with an increased MVI risk. After multivariable adjustment, SUVmax retained independent predictive value (OR = 2.140, 95% CI: 1.244-3.681, P = 0.006), whereas the multivariable evidence for TLR was derived from a single study and required further validation. AUC values for SUVmax and radiomics score (Rad-score) were 0.819 (95% CI: 0.739-0.899) and 0.809 (95% CI: 0.762-0.857), respectively, with relatively balanced values for sensitivity, specificity, and negative likelihood ratio. CONCLUSION: The available evidence supports SUVmax as one of the metabolic markers for preoperative MVI risk assessment in HCC, with Rad-score similar to SUVmax in diagnostic discrimination. The complementary value of the two markers was not demonstrated by this Meta-analysis, but rather derived from inferences proposed by external studies. Moreover, because the included radiomics studies did not report a pooled effect size for the combined model integrating SUVmax and Rad-score, a Meta-analysis targeting this model is currently not feasible. Therefore, the complementarity of SUVmax and Rad-score should be regarded as a hypothesis to be tested. In the future, multicenter, prospective radiomics studies with rigorous external validation are warranted to further explore a combined prediction model based on SUVmax and Rad-score. On this basis, an integrated assessment workflow should be gradually established, by which preoperative decisions are guided.

title: Primary pulmonary mucoepidermoid carcinoma: a case report.
abstract: Primary pulmonary mucoepidermoid carcinoma(PMEC) is a rare salivary gland-type malignancy, accounting for fewer than 0.2% of all primary lung tumors. We report herein a 61-year-old male patient with PMEC who was admitted for a space-occupying lesion in the left upper lobe and had a 20-year smoking history. Contrast-enhanced chest CT and positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT) revealed a central space-occupying lesion in the left hilum with distal obstructive inflammation. Flexible bronchoscopy revealed a nodular mass in the left main bronchus. Biopsy histopathology combined with immunohistochemistry confirmed the diagnosis of PMEC. Immunohistochemistry showed CK7 (+), P63 (-), P40 (-), CD117 (focal+), TTF-1 (-), NapsinA (-), and Ki-67 (7%+). Molecular testing identified a CRTC1-MAML2 gene fusion, whereas no classic driver gene mutations (e.g., EGFR or KRAS) were detected. PD-L1 expression was negative, and the tumor mutational burden (TMB) was low. The low Ki-67 index and positive MAML2 fusion in this case suggest a low-grade PMEC with a relatively favorable prognosis. The present study discusses the clinicopathological features, imaging findings, molecular diagnosis, and therapeutic advances of PMEC, along with a review of the relevant literature, aiming to increase clinical awareness of this rare disease.

title: Intracranial phosphaturic mesenchymal tumor mimicking meningioma and causing tumor-induced osteomalacia: a case report.
abstract: A 32-yr-old woman presented with a 2-year history of progressive bone pain, proximal muscle weakness, worsening ambulation, and bilateral hip insufficiency fractures without preceding trauma. Laboratory evaluation revealed severe hypophosphatemia (1.1 mg/dL), elevated bone-specific alkaline phosphatase, progressive secondary hyperparathyroidism, and inappropriately elevated circulating FGF-23, with fasting paired serum and urine studies confirming renal phosphate wasting (tubular maximum phosphate reabsorption per glomerular filtration rate 1.88 mg/dL; fractional excretion of phosphate 14.6%), consistent with tumor-induced osteomalacia (TIO). Functional imaging with 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT demonstrated intense tracer uptake in a small anterior cranial lesion. Brain MRI revealed a dural-based olfactory groove lesion interpreted radiographically as a meningioma. Selective venous sampling demonstrated a cranial-to-peripheral gradient in intact FGF-23 consistent with drainage from the anterior cranial fossa. Surgical resection produced postoperative normalization of FGF-23 and rapid correction of hypophosphatemia. Histology showed meningioma-like architecture with whorls and psammoma bodies, but expanded molecular testing did not identify canonical meningioma-associated alterations, and DNA methylation profiling classified the lesion as a mesenchymal neoplasm not elsewhere classified and fusion negative. FGF-23 in situ hybridization was positive, and the final surgical pathology diagnosis was mesenchymal tumor favoring phosphaturic mesenchymal tumor over meningioma. This case illustrates how a mesenchymal tumor arising in the meninges can mimic meningioma radiographically and histologically while producing the endocrine phenotype of TIO.

title: Kinetically controlled proton removal via bio-inspired hybrid bilayer membrane functionalized electrode for ethylene glycol oxidation to generate C2 products.
abstract: As a cornerstone of the circular carbon economy, the upcycling of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) relies on efficient monomer recovery and subsequent high-value transformation. While PET can be effectively broken down into ethylene glycol (EG) via scalable depolymerization techniques such as hydrolysis, alcoholysis, or pyrolysis, the subsequent electrochemical ethylene glycol oxidation reaction (EgOR) faces a significant selectivity bottleneck. This reaction is governed by complex proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) pathways that typically favor C-C bond cleavage, resulting in low-value C1 products like formic acid and CO2. In this work, we overcome these limitations by employing a bio-inspired hybrid bilayer membrane (HBM) functionalized electrode to exert kinetic control over the proton removal rate. By precisely modulating the electrocatalytic microenvironment at the electrode interface, the HBM suppresses over-oxidation and steers the reaction toward the targeted generation of C2 products. We demonstrate the selective production of glycolic acid, a premium chemical in the cosmetics industry with a market value exceeding 25 times that of the EG feedstock. These results establish that regulating the kinetics of proton transfer via HBM technology is a transformative strategy for controlling reaction selectivity in complex oxidation pathways. This approach offers a potentially scalable, renewable-energy-powered route for upcycling plastic waste derivatives into high-value chemical outputs, providing significant translational value for sustainable resource recovery.

title: Metal-Dependent Coordination Geometry Controls Autolytic Amide Bond Cleavage to Enable Prodrug Activation.
mesh: Prodrugs; Humans; Amides; Coordination Complexes; Antineoplastic Agents; Animals; Hydrolysis; Mice
abstract: We introduce a peptide prodrug activation strategy that employs the trivalent Lewis-acidic metal ions Ga3+, Fe3+, In3+, and Co3+, chelated by triazacyclononanediacetic acid monoamides. The metal chelates trigger rate-tunable, metal-mediated, autolytic amide bond cleavage (TMAC) adjacent to N-methylated and canonical amino acids. Our studies reveal that the four TMAC-compatible metal ions induce amide bond hydrolysis with divergent pH dependence and mechanistic pathways. We subsequently linked Ga3+, Fe3+, In3+, and Co3+ complexes to the N-terminus of a potent cytotoxic cargo, monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), to produce the proof-of-concept prodrug PD1. In vitro toxicity studies establish IC50 values in HeLa and PC-3 cells that broadly correlate with complex cleavage rates; the metal ion-free PD1 conjugate, the Zn-PD1 complex, as well as the Ga3+, Fe3+, In3+, and Co3+ chelate hydrolysis products alone confer no toxicity. Attachment of a cancer-targeting peptide to the metal chelate, furnishing PD2, enables targeted delivery of the therapeutic payload in vivo, compatible with noninvasive nuclear imaging using positron emission tomography with 68Ga or single-photon computed tomography with 111In. The corresponding natGa-PD2 complex selectively suppressed tumor growth in vivo with minimal off-target toxicity. These studies establish metal identity as a general design parameter for programming amide bond cleavage and introduce TMAC as a versatile platform to engender peptide prodrugs with tunable release kinetics.

title: Radiomics-Based Outcome Prediction in Transarterial Radioembolization (TARE) of Hepatic Malignancies: A Systematic Review and Quality Appraisal.
abstract: Background: Transarterial radioembolization (TARE) with Yttrium-90 (90Y) microspheres is an established locoregional treatment for primary and secondary hepatic malignancies. Treatment response is heterogeneous, and accurate pre-procedural prediction of outcome remains a clinical challenge. Radiomics, defined as the high-throughput extraction of quantitative imaging features, may capture subvisual tumour heterogeneity that might be predictive of response, therefore enabling individualised patient selection and treatment planning. Objectives: To systematically review the current evidence on radiomics-based models derived from pre- and post-procedural imaging for predicting treatment response and survival outcomes in patients with primary and secondary hepatic lesions that were treated with TARE, and to evaluate the methodological quality of included studies. Methods: A systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science. Studies reporting radiomics, texture analysis, dosiomics, or machine learning applied to imaging in patients with hepatic lesions treated with TARE, with at least one reported performance metric, were included. Methodological quality was assessed using the Radiomics Quality Score (RQS) and risk of bias and applicability using the Prediction model Risk Of Bias ASsessment Tool (PROBAST). Due to substantial heterogeneity, a narrative synthesis was performed. Results: Twenty-one studies encompassing 1734 patients were included (up to 73 patients may be counted twice because two cohorts overlap). Studies evaluated patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC; n = 12), intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCC; n = 2), colorectal cancer liver metastases (CLMs; n = 3), and mixed tumour cohorts (n = 4). Imaging modalities included MRI (n = 9), CT (n = 5), 18F-FDG PET or PET/CT (n = 3), 90Y PET or SPECT (n = 2), cone-beam CT (n = 1), and CT perfusion (n = 1). All studies were retrospective, including two post hoc analyses of randomised trial cohorts, and none used external validation. Eighteen studies reported an area under the curve (AUC). The highest reported AUC ranged from 0.71 to 0.90 in eight studies with no validation, from 0.73 to 1.00 in six studies using internal cross-validation, and from 0.80 to 0.90 in four studies using an internal hold-out set. title: Aortic Endograft Infection After COVID-19: A Single-Centre Case Series and a Proposed Descriptive Clinical-Radiological PET/CT Staging Framework.
abstract: Background: Aortic endograft infection (AEI) after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) is rare but life-threatening. The Management of Aortic Graft Infection Collaboration (MAGIC) criteria define infection, but there is no standard way to report the extent of infection. We describe patients who developed AEI after coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) and propose a descriptive clinical-radiological PET/CT staging framework. Methods: Retrospective, single-centre case series of EVAR patients who underwent [18F] fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (FDG PET/CT) between 2020 and 2023. Six index patients (Group A) were managed for AEI after PCR-confirmed COVID-19. Five reference patients without COVID-19, imaged during the same period for suspected infection at another site (Group B, n = 2) or malignancy (Group C, n = 3), were included to describe endograft uptake in the absence of AEI; they were not matched controls. Each patient was classified according to MAGIC, with the finding supporting each criterion recorded. Each endograft was assigned a descriptive clinical-radiological stage (0-III): Stages 0-II were defined by PET/CT uptake pattern and anatomical extent, and Stage III by an additional imaging-defined (e.g., endograft limb thrombosis) or clinical (sepsis) complication, recorded separately. Results: Mean age was 76 years (9 men). Of the six index patients, one (Case 6, organism cultured from the explanted endograft) met the MAGIC definition of diagnosed AEI and five met that of suspected AEI. All six presented with fever, and every index patient had at least one additional source of bacteraemia or cause of immunosuppression, including corticosteroids given for COVID-19 pneumonia. Five had iliopsoas abscess. Four index endografts were classified as Stage III (clinical complication, sepsis, in all four; imaging-defined complication, endograft limb thrombosis, also in one) and two as Stage II; all five reference endografts were Stage 0. The median interval from COVID-19 to AEI diagnosis was 14 months (IQR 10-16), and from EVAR to PET/CT 15 months (IQR 4-35). Three index patients died (two infection- or aorta-related), and all three Group C patients died of malignancy progression. Conclusions: This case series describes late AEI, frequently with iliopsoas involvement, in patients with prior COVID-19 and multiple other risk facto

title: Multimodal Detection of a Minute Uterine Cornual Lesion in Cervical Clear Cell Carcinoma.
abstract: Cervical clear cell carcinoma (CCC) is a rare human papillomavirus (HPV)-independent adenocarcinoma. A 73-year-old woman presented with postmenopausal bleeding. Ultrasonography demonstrated a cervical mass and a 5.0 × 5.0 mm right cornual nodule. On 3.0-T magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), the cornual lesion measured 5.2 × 5.3 mm and, like the cervical tumor, showed high signal intensity on diffusion-weighted imaging (b = 1000 s/mm2). 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) demonstrated intense uptake in the cervical mass (30.6 × 29.2 × 41.2 mm; SUVmax 10.4) and in the spatially separate right cornual nodule (5.2 × 5.1 mm; SUVmax 14.6), without FDG-avid nodal or distant metastatic disease. The concordant identification of the cornual lesion by ultrasonography, MRI, and PET/CT prompted multidisciplinary reassessment and radical hysterectomy to obtain definitive pathological characterization of both lesions. Histopathology demonstrated clear cell carcinoma at both sites; however, because molecular, genomic, or clonality analyses were not performed, their biological relationship remains uncertain. All 30 examined lymph nodes and the surgical margins were negative. The cervical primary was staged as pT1b3 pN0 cM0 (FIGO 2018 stage IB3). The patient received four cycles of postoperative chemotherapy with paclitaxel plus cisplatin. At 14 months after surgery, gynecological examination and pelvic MRI showed no evidence of recurrence. This case highlights the complementary roles of ultrasonography, MRI, and 18F-FDG PET/CT in characterizing a minute spatially separate uterine lesion while underscoring the need for cautious interpretation when the relationship between lesions cannot be established.

title: Is PET/CT Useful in Detecting Pneumocystis jirovecii Colonization in Patients with Primary Lung Cancer?
abstract: Background/Objectives:Pneumocystis jirovecii colonization induces persistent low-grade pulmonary inflammation, which may alter fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) uptake in positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT). We aimed to evaluate whether asymptomatic infection influences the maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) or clinicopathological parameters of primary lung cancer. Methods: In this prospective single-center observational study, 107 consecutive patients undergoing surgical resection for primary lung cancer were enrolled. Preoperative FDG PET/CT scans were obtained within four weeks prior to surgery. Intraoperative respiratory secretions and lung tissue samples were analyzed for P. jirovecii, using nested polymerase chain reaction (nested-PCR) targeting the mitochondrial large subunit rRNA gene. Propensity score matching (PSM) adjusting for age, sex, and body mass index was performed across 1:1, 1:2, and 1:3 matching models. Results:Pneumocystis jirovecii colonization was confirmed in 12 of 107 patients (11.21%). In the unadjusted cohort, no significant differences in primary lesion SUVmax were identified between positive and negative patients (10.38 ± 6.50 vs. 8.86 ± 6.58, p = 0.411), nor across matched models (1:1: p = 0.555; 1:2: p = 0.951; 1:3: p = 0.926). Following PSM, patients without colonization exhibited significantly larger maximum tumor diameters in both 1:2 (30.71 ± 19.23 vs. 18.25 ± 6.63 mm, p = 0.035) and 1:3 matching models (29.08 ± 17.47 vs. 18.25 ± 6.63 mm, p = 0.035). Conclusions: We did not find any association between P. jirovecii colonization and preoperative metabolic tumor staging on FDG PET/CT. However, asymptomatic carriage was associated with smaller primary tumor dimensions following propensity adjustment in 1:2 and 1:3 matching models, warranting further exploration of host-fungal interactions within the pulmonary tumor microenvironment.

title: PemToxTrial: An Observational Study of PEMetrexed-Associated Severe HematoTOXicity in Lung Adenocarcinoma with Bone Metastases.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Pemetrexed, an antifolate, is a standard therapy for lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). Since folic acid is vital for nucleic acid metabolism, disrupting its pathway affects both tumor cells and regenerating healthy cells. The PemToxTrial examined the impact of pemetrexed on severe hematotoxicity and mortality. METHODS: This retrospective analysis included 136 LUAD patients (UICC8 stage IVA/B) receiving palliative treatment. Ninety-two patients received pemetrexed-based therapy, while 44 received pemetrexed-free treatment (68 and 38 with immune-checkpoint inhibitors). Bone metastasis (BM) was present in 47 patients in the pemetrexed group and 22 in the comparison group. The primary endpoint was grade III-V hematotoxicity; secondary endpoints included mortality, progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS). Hematologic outcomes following a subsequent change in clinical practice were prospectively assessed in a post-implementation cohort of 15 patients with bone-metastatic LUAD receiving pemetrexed-free regimens. RESULTS: Median age was 66 years, 59.6% were male and median follow-up was 13.5 months. Grade III-V hematotoxicity was most frequent (81%) in patients with BM receiving pemetrexed (n = 47), significantly higher than in other subgroups (p < 0.0001). Mortality was also increased in this group (66% vs. 29%, p < 0.0001), with hematotoxicity directly contributing to death in 42% versus 11.5% of cases. PFS was significantly inferior (5.2 vs. 8.6 months). Multivariable analysis identified BM as the only independent predictor of severe hematotoxicity and mortality. Only a mutational burden of ≥4 potential driver alterations was associated with inferior PFS. Bone-derived total lesion glycolysis (TLG) on PET-CT strongly correlated with high-grade hematotoxicity (p < 0.0001). CONCLUSIONS: The PemToxTrial identified a strong association between pemetrexed exposure, bone metastases, and severe hematotoxicity, supporting further prospective evaluation of bone metastasis status as a potential clinical risk factor for treatment-associated hematotoxicity.

title: Real-World Utilization of Tissue-Free ctDNA MRD Testing in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Across Asia-Pacific and the Middle East: A Descriptive Cohort Analysis and Illustrative Case Series.
abstract: Introduction: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA)-based molecular residual disease (MRD) testing is emerging as a tool to refine relapse risk and guide surveillance after curative-intent therapy for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Tissue-free (plasma-only) MRD assays may improve feasibility where tumor tissue is limited. Prospective and trial-embedded studies have established that ctDNA MRD detected after curative-intent therapy is prognostic for recurrence in NSCLC, but how tissue-free MRD testing is deployed in routine care in Asia-Pacific and the Middle East (AMEA) has not been described. We characterized ordering patterns and first-test positivity in an AMEA cohort. In this descriptive cohort (159 NSCLC patients; 257 samples), 40.9% of patients underwent more than one MRD test, with a median interval of 4.9 months between the first two tests; first-test MRD positivity was 15.7% (25/159; 95% CI 10.9-22.2) with rates of 0% (0/9; 95% CI 0.0-29.9), 8.8% (5/57; 95% CI 3.8-18.9), 21.5% (17/79; 95% CI 13.9-31.8) and 21.4% (3/14; 95% CI 7.6-47.6), respectively, across stages I, II, III, and oligometastatic stage IV disease. No hypothesis testing was performed, and the stage I and oligometastatic stage IV subgroups are small, so the confidence intervals overlap widely and apparent between-stage differences should not be interpreted as a stage effect. Case Presentation: Six illustrative cases involving patients with stage II-IVB describe the use of MRD testing in routine clinical care. The cases were selected purposively, not consecutively, to span the contexts in which the results were interpreted: a positive result shortly before radiographic nodal recurrence (Case 1); a positive result during long-term adjuvant osimertinib preceding isolated mediastinal relapse (Case 2); a transient positive result with subsequent clearance and radiographic regression (Case 3); a positive result that prompted PET-CT revealing occult metastatic disease (Case 4); serially negative results concordant with sustained radiographic remission (Case 5); and a positive result that prompted comprehensive genomic profiling identifying an actionable KRAS G12C alteration (Case 6). title: Prognostic Value of Baseline High-Uptake PSMA Tumor Volume Fraction in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer Patients Treated with [177Lu]Lu-PSMA Radioligand Therapy.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Lutetium-177 prostate-specific membrane antigen radioligand therapy ([177Lu]Lu-PSMA-RLT) is an effective treatment for patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), but no validated PSMA-PET/CT-based biomarker currently identifies patients at risk of early treatment failure. The aim of this study was to assess whether semi-quantitative PSMA-PET/CT parameters, in particular the fraction of PSMA-positive tumor volume with high uptake, are associated with early biochemical progression (EBP) and PSA50 response and secondarily with PSA-PFS and OS. Methods: Semiquantitative PSMA-PET parameters comprised reference lesion SUVmax (RL-SUVmax), SUVmean, total PSMA tumor volume (tPSMA-TV), tPSMA-TV above a fixed SUV threshold of 20 (tPSMA-TV20), the percentage of tPSMA-TV20 within tPSMA-TV (tPSMA-TV%), total lesion quotient (TLQ), TLQ20, and rTLQ%. The co-primary endpoints were EBP, defined as PSA progression according to the PCWG3 criteria within 4 months of the start of treatment, and PSA50 response, defined as a reduction in PSA of at least 50% compared with baseline. PSA-PFS (PCWG3-defined PSA progression or death from any cause) and OS were secondary endpoints. Results: 63 patients were retrospectively included (median follow-up, 20.9 months). In univariable analyses, higher baseline tPSMA-TV% was significantly associated with lower odds of EBP (OR per 10% increase, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.57-0.87; p = 0.001) and higher odds of PSA50 response (OR, 1.31; 95% CI, 1.07-1.61; p = 0.009). It was associated with longer PSA-PFS (HR, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.67-0.84; p < 0.001) and longer OS (HR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.72-0.91; p < 0.001). Exploratory ROC analysis identified a tPSMA-TV% cut-off of 47.54% for EBP (AUC, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.57-0.86]; sensitivity, 0.61; specificity, 0.93), although this threshold requires external validation. In exploratory models including tPSMA-TV and SUVmean, tPSMA-TV% remained associated with PSA-PFS and OS but not with EBP or PSA50 response. Conclusions: Baseline tPSMA-TV% was associated with EBP, PSA50 response, PSA-PFS and OS in mCRPC patients undergoing [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-RLT, and these associations remained after adjustment for baseline PSA and metastatic presentation. tPSMA-TV% is a candidate prognostic imaging biomarker that requires external validation.

title: [18F]FDG PET/CT-Derived Metabolic Characteristics and Tumour-Infiltrating Lymphocytes for Predicting Axillary Response to Neoadjuvant Chemo-(Immuno)Therapy in Clinically Node-Positive Breast Cancer.
abstract: Background: Accurate axillary response prediction is clinically relevant in clinically node-positive (cN+) breast cancer patients treated with neoadjuvant chemo-(immuno)therapy (NAC). This study evaluated the value of [18F]FDG PET/CT-derived metabolic characteristics and tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) to predict axillary pathologic complete response (pCR). Second, the association between [18F]FDG PET/CT-derived metabolic characteristics and TILs was evaluated. Methods: This retrospective study included cN+ breast cancer patients treated with NAC and axillary surgery from the prospective multicentre RISAS trial (NCT02800317). Baseline [18F]FDG PET/CT-derived metabolic activity of the breast tumour, axillary lymph node metastases (ALNMs), and spleen was assessed, together with TILs measured in the breast tumour and ALNMs. TILs were classified as low (<10%) versus high (≥10%). Associations were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analysis. Results: Of 135 patients, 46 (34.1%) achieved axillary pCR. Higher liver mean tumour-to-background ratio (2.7 vs. 1.9, p = 0.042), trends towards higher breast and ALNM maximum standardised uptake value (SUVmax), lower splenic SUVmax and high breast tumour TILs were associated with axillary pCR. Multivariable logistic regression combining tumour grade, subtype, maximum spleen-to-liver ratio, and breast tumour TILs yielded an apparent area under the curve of 0.80 [95%CI 0.73-0.88]. Higher ALNM SUVmax and SUVmean (10.5 vs. 6.3, p = 0.024; 6.4 vs. 3.7, p = 0.015) and lower splenic SUVmean (2.6 vs. 3.1, p = 0.035) were associated with high breast tumour TILs. Conclusions: A model combining clinicopathological, metabolic, and immune-related characteristics may be informative for predicting axillary response to NAC but did not perform better than clinicopathological characteristics alone. Future studies should evaluate whether accurate prediction models can support safe axillary treatment de-escalation.

title: Optic Nerve Sheath Meningiomas: A Narrative Review of Clinical Features, Imaging Advances, and Current Management.
abstract: Optic nerve sheath meningioma (ONSM) is a rare orbital tumor that can pose a significant threat to visual function due to its close relationship with the optic nerve and surrounding vascular structures. Early and accurate diagnosis is essential to preserve vision and guide individualized management. The objective of this narrative review is to provide a comprehensive overview of the current evidence on the clinical presentation, diagnostic evaluation, imaging characteristics, and management of ONSM, with a particular focus on recent advances in imaging techniques and their implications for clinical decision-making. This review synthesizes current knowledge on clinical presentation, diagnostic workup, and evolving treatment strategies for ONSM, with particular emphasis on advanced imaging modalities. Magnetic resonance imaging remains the cornerstone of diagnosis, yet functional imaging, especially somatostatin receptor--based techniques such as 68GaDOTATATE PET/CT have shown potential as a useful adjunct in the diagnostic evaluation of ONSM, especially for assessing tumor characteristics, extent, and treatment planning in selected cases. We discuss the emerging role of DOTATATE imaging in differentiating ONSM from other optic nerve and orbital pathologies, as well as its potential application in monitoring therapeutic response. We also highlight contemporary management approaches, including fractionated radiotherapy and the selective role of surgical intervention, underscoring the importance of multidisciplinary decision-making in optimizing visual outcomes. Emerging molecular insights from meningioma research may inform future therapeutic strategies for ONSM; however, clinical evidence specific to ONSM remains limited.

title: Spatio-Temporal Patterns and Ecological Implications of Microplastic Contamination in Benthic Fish from the Tongkou River, China.
abstract: Microplastic pollution in rivers is a critical environmental threat that harms aquatic life. To understand the abundance, physical characteristics, and polymer types of microplastics, this study examined the intestinal tract of four fish groups (three individual species: Saurogobio dabryi, Squalidus argentatus, and Hemibarbus labeo; and a pooled group of four loach species: Paramisgurnus dabryanus, Triplophysa bleekeri, Oreias dabryi, and Paracobitis variegatus) collected from the Tongkou River in October 2023 and November 2024 using tissue digestion methods across different river sections. The results revealed that every single fish contained microplastics, with contamination levels significantly higher downstream than upstream. Over the study period, total microplastic counts dropped by 32 percent from 2023 to 2024. Most of the collected pellets were thin threads and small fragments measuring under one millimeter, composed mainly of common plastics and cellulose. These findings demonstrate that freshwater fish are widely exposed to small plastic fibers, showing distinct geographic and yearly trends. Ultimately, this research provides essential baseline data to help authorities develop effective strategies to reduce plastic pollution in freshwater ecosystems and protect aquatic wildlife.

title: Beyond a Universal Cut-Off: [18F]FET-PET Metrics for Distinguishing High-Grade Glioma Recurrence from Treatment-Related Changes.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Differentiating tumour recurrence from treatment-related changes (TRC) after multimodal treatment of high-grade gliomas (HGGs) remains challenging because of the overlap in imaging findings on conventional magnetic resonance. This study compared the diagnostic performance of the main static semiquantitative O-(2-[18F]fluoroethyl)-L-tyrosine positron emission tomography ([18F]FET-PET) parameters and assessed the diagnostic contribution of qualitative tracer uptake. Methods: This retrospective single-centre study included 77 scans from 61 adult patients with previously resected and chemoradiotherapy-treated HGGs undergoing [18F]FET-PET for suspected recurrence. Standardised uptake values (SUVs), tumour-to-background ratios (TBRs), and metabolic tumour volume (MTV) were analysed. Recurrence was determined using a composite histopathological and clinical-radiological reference standard. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis, Youden-derived cut-offs and DeLong comparisons. Internal validation was performed by using patient-grouped five-fold cross-validation, in which cut-offs were re-derived within each training partition and applied to the held-out partition. Results: Forty-nine scans were classified as recurrence and 28 as TRC. All semiquantitative parameters except MTV were significantly higher in recurrent disease after false-discovery-rate correction. TBR mean ratio showed the highest accuracy (AUC, 0.80; cut-off, 1.85; sensitivity, 77.6%; specificity, 75.0%), followed by SUV max (AUC, 0.793). Neither prespecified comparison among TBR parameters was significant. The presence of pathological uptake achieved 100% sensitivity, 42.9% specificity, 100% NPV, and 79.2% accuracy. MTV was non-discriminative (AUC, 0.499). SUV max differed significantly between scanners (p = 0.008). Conclusions: Static semiquantitative [18F]FET-PET parameters, except MTV, showed comparable moderate-to-good performance for distinguishing recurrence from TRC. TBRmean may represent a pragmatic primary marker due to its background normalisation reduction of scanner-related variability. Guideline-recommended thresholds should be regarded as reference values requiring local validation and, when appropriate, centre- and protocol-specific calibration.
